Before this PR, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` inherited V1's implementation and the call worked. findings.title: Event listener feature-flag mismatch causes UnsupportedOperationException when both V1 and V2 FGAP are enabled
findings.body: The event listener body is wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, but inside it calls `management(...)` which dispatches to MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. With the new `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` override, that path returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` now throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Before this PR, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` inherited V1's implementation and the call worked. As a result, in a realm where both `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` and `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` are enabled, any `ClientRemovedEvent` (or `RoleRemovedEvent`/`GroupRemovedEvent` whose management path is also impacted) will raise `UnsupportedOperationException`. The check should be either `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ && !ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`, or the calls into the V2 evaluator should be guarded so that the unsupported operation is not invoked when V2 is in effect.

findings.title: Possible NPE in hasPermission when the "all-clients" resource does not exist
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, when no per-client resource exists, the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. That method can return null (e.g., schema not yet initialized, `supportsAuthorizationSchema` returns false, unknown resource type, or `findByName` returns no row). The result is then passed unchecked to `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`, which dereferences the resource (e.g., to read its id) and will throw NullPointerException. A null check is required before invoking `findByResource`.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission only enumerates the "all-clients" resource and misses individual client resources
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` iterates with `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. Only the type-resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` (with type "Clients") matches this query, because `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates per-client resources without setting the `type` field (the `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` call never sets a type). Therefore (a) when a user has permission only via a per-client resource, `getClientsWithPermission` returns an empty set, and (b) when the user has an "all-clients" grant, the result contains the literal name "Clients" instead of the actual client IDs in the realm. Either the per-client resources must be created with `type = CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`, or the enumeration should iterate all client resources (e.g., `resourceStore.findByName(server, ...)` for each client, or by a different store query).

findings.title: No test exercises the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope for clients
findings.body: The new `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` (and its corresponding schema scope `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`) is declared on the interface and implemented, but `PermissionClientTest` does not contain a test case that grants `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` and verifies the associated behavior is allowed, nor a negative case. Only `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` are exercised through `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`. A dedicated test should be added so the new scope is covered by the test suite.

findings.title: Several imports and a private helper are unused
findings.body: The imports `org.jboss.logging.Logger`, `org.keycloak.authorization.common.ClientModelIdentity`, `org.keycloak.authorization.common.DefaultEvaluationContext`, `org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope`, `org.keycloak.models.RealmModel`, `org.keycloak.representations.AccessToken`, the static import `org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.permissions.AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, and the private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` (plus the `Map`, `Collection`, `List` transitive uses it drags in) are not referenced anywhere in the file. The unused `private static final Logger logger` field and the dead `getEvaluationContext` helper should be removed to keep the class focused on the implementation that is actually wired up.
